prompt:
Make one opaque pixel-art eye atlas for common portrait NPC083 ANGRY, using this single image as the exact source/reference. Canvas: exact 2 columns × 2 rows, equal cells, overall aspect ratio 64:35 (about 1.83:1), each cell represents one native 64×35 eye-area crop. No gutters, margins, labels, borders, text, or extra panels. Row-major cells: top-left LEFT/open, top-right RIGHT/open, bottom-left LEFT/half, bottom-right RIGHT/half. Both eyes glance together in each cell.

Preserve this exact angry face, its tense brow expression, eye spacing, source palette, pixel scale, compact iris shape, and source eyelid contours. Keep the eye aperture exactly as shown for each phase: open cells use the source open aperture; half cells use the source half-lid aperture and coverage. Do not widen or reshape either opening, lift the upper lids, change brows, or enlarge eyes. Change only the compact irises and pupils by a gentle horizontal glance of about one native pixel: toward the viewer's left in LEFT cells, toward the viewer's right in RIGHT cells. Keep both pupils fully within the existing openings and partly bounded by the source lids. Retain the exact muted source iris/sclera/pupil colors; no bright white bands, broad pale patches, increased contrast, oversized or round irises, or shiny highlights. Keep glints tiny and subdued at source intensity.

Do not alter the forehead, hair, skin, nose, face, background, crop, or other details. Crisp native pixel edges; no smoothing, blur, antialiasing, resampling, invented colors, or painterly detail. Return only the requested four-cell atlas; no closed or vertical gaze.
